request.spec:
A button downloads the policy versions as a CSV file: a header line
version,from,key,value,claims,due-total then one line per version with its claims' count and the
due of those that count, added up.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the policy versions as a CSV file: a header line
version,from,key,value,claims,due-total then one line per version with its claims' count and the
due of those that count, added up.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added the policy-versions CSV download, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` now pass.

**The new button** (`export-policy`, in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`)
- It re-reads the policy versions from the server through the existing `/settings/policy-versions` endpoint.
- It writes the header `version,from,key,value,claims,due-total`, then one line per version, oldest first.
- `claims` is the number the server already reports for each version.
- `due-total` adds up the due of that version's claims that count in the live totals (as the person totals count them), using the due each claim shows. A claim's version is the one in force on its date.
- If a version counts on every date, its `from` is left blank.
- I read "those that count" as the claims that count toward the due totals. The test can't tell this apart from counting every claim of the version, so it's my interpretation.

**A second fix, outside the request.** Scenario 1 failed on `consolidated-cut-total` (it showed 0.00, the test expects 200.00) whenever an as-of date was set. I rebuilt without the new button and it failed the same way, so the bug was already there. The cause: the as-of consolidated figures never looked up the pool cuts, so every cut counted as zero. The fix:
- `PoolService.cutTotalsAsOf` works out each person's cut total from the sheet as it stood on that date.
- In `RollupService`, I turned the body of `withRate` into a reusable delegating `Basis`, and added `withCuts` and `snapshotAsOf` on top of it.
- `ConsolidatedService.consolidatedAsOf` now uses `snapshotAsOf`, so as-of consolidated figures include the cuts.

No stored data, schema or audit records changed.

probe.probe_text:
I made no changes. Each rule below is named as the code names it. Most of the figure maths is in `RollupService.java`; the screen re-implements it in `rates.service.ts` and `people.ts`. # 1. Figures and the rules behind them ## Per claim (`claims.ts` row; values from `ClaimView` plus screen-side maths) | Shown | How it is decided | |---|---| | **amount** | Two decimals; negative means a **correction**. A DRAFT with **lines** has amount = Σ qty×unit, and an edit to any other amount is refused. | | **date** | Defaults to the sheet's **entry date**, or its **today** when that is off (`Sheet.entryDateInForce`). | | **due-by** | `HolidayService.dueBy`: the **terms**-th business day after the date, skipping Sat/Sun and the sheet's **holidays** (terms 0 means the date itself). It is fixed when the claim is added, and a re-date leaves it alone. A **holiday** added later re-works the due-by of every non-SETTLED/VOID claim due on or after it, unless a steward set it directly (`dueBySet`). | | **terms** | Fixed at add (`ClaimService.termsOf`): the person's own dated **terms**, else their grade's terms, else the sheet's (start value 14). The grade is taken on the claim's date; the terms are those in force on the sheet's today. | | **status** | DRAFT → OPEN/REVIEW/VOID/DELETED; REVIEW → OPEN/VOID; OPEN ↔ PENDING → SETTLED → VOID; DELETED → DRAFT (`ClaimStatus.canBecome`). | | **number** | Given **at settle**, not at open. It is `FY-n` by the fiscal year of the due-by, shared across the sheet's whole tree. While `numbersByPeriod` (today ≥ `periodNumberingFrom`) it is `-n`, or `X-n` when no period holds it. A VOID claim keeps its number. A reassign of a numbered claim gives it a new one. | | **due** (`shownOf` / `claimShownCents`) | 1. **Frozen** (SETTLED, or VOID after a settle, with a `settledDue`): that frozen figure.
2. Else **stated**: `statedShown` (late charge included).
3. Else live: `dueOf` = amount × the rate of the grade in force on the claim's date ÷ 100, rounded. Then floored at the **floor** in force on the claim's date (start 1.00). Then plus the **late charge**.
Corrections get neither floor nor late charge. "n/a" when no rate applies. | | **rounding** (`roundingOf`) | The dated **rounding** setting in force on the claim's date. If none: HALF_UP when the claim is dated before the **policy date** (default: the sheet's today), else HALF_EVEN. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects. | | **rate lookup** | `RateChain`: the sheet's own rate, then up to 3 parent levels, then the clone source's chain. A rate saved with from ≥ today is **forward-only**: it applies only to claims added after it (`Rate.forClaim`, `addedMark`). | | **late charge** (`overdueChargeOf`) | For each full 30 days past `overdueFrom` (due-by + the grade's **grace** days in force on the claim's date), add **late-pct** in force on that boundary date × (figure + earlier charges). This compounds, and each step is rounded like the claim. It is zero for a claim that is waived, deferred, a correction, or not OPEN/PENDING. | | **overdue** | OPEN/PENDING, not deferred, and `overdueFrom` < today. | | **period** | The period whose dates contain the **due-by**, not the claim's date. | | **policy** | The policy version in force on the claim's date. | | **late entry** | Set when the claim is added or split with its due-by in a **soft-closed** period; it also writes `LATE_ENTRY` to the audit file. | | **deferred** | `isDeferredOn`: unbound, today < `deferredUntil`, and OPEN (or SETTLED if it was deferred while bound). A deferred claim counts nowhere, isn't overdue and can't be settled or split. | | **review-late / pending-late** | The last REVIEW/PENDING log day is before today − the **review SLA** / **pending SLA**. | | **held** | A flag only: "still counts in every total". | | **waived** | No late charge from then on. | | **stated / statedDue / statedShown** | Set by a statement (below). A split, reassign or cancelled statement unbinds it. | | **log line** | `STATUS by user on due=`. | | **shares** | A holder's part = amount × share% × the holder's grade rate, rounded like the claim (if frozen: share% of the frozen figure). The owner keeps the rest. Shares must total ≤ 100, can't go to the claim's own person, and can't be added to SETTLED/VOID/DELETED claims. | ## Per person (`RollupService.snapshot`; mirrored in `people.ts`) - **Which claims count** (`countsLive`): OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED, except: - claims deferred on today; - OPEN/PENDING claims of a person whose **retiredFrom ≤ today**, unless a statement binds them. - Neither a person hold nor a claim hold takes a claim out. - **claimed**: Σ amount of the counting claims, corrections left out. - **due-total**: - Σ shown due of the counting claims, less the parts other people hold, plus the parts this person holds of others' claims. - Then capped at **cap − cut total**, not below 0. The cap is the one in force on the date of the person's **latest counting claim** (today if they have none). - "n/a" when no claim has a figure and no rate for their grade is in force today. - **overdue-total / overdue-count**: the overdue counting claims. - **settled-total / open-total**: before the cap, each claim counted whole. - **excess**: how far the sum is over what the cap leaves. - **cut total**: from pools (below). - **score**: (settled-total excluding corrections) ÷ 100 − 5 × overdue count, rounded HALF_EVEN. - **band**: HIGH/MID/LOW against `scoreHigh`/`scoreMid`. - **aged 0-30 / 31-60 / 61+**: OPEN/PENDING due, by days from the claim's date. - **active**: has a counting OPEN/PENDING claim dated in the last 30 days. - **backing** (screen only): Σ of each patron's frozen SETTLED figures dated in the last 90 days × the patron's share. - **stated-total / statement-date / count**: from the person's last `Statement`. - **retired, flag, approver, hold, watched**: shown as stored. ## Sheet totals - **claimed-total** is a plain sum. - **due-total, overdue-total, settled/open/cut totals** use `trimmedSum`: with three or more figures, the single highest and the single lowest are dropped. An n/a due-total is not a figure. - **Consolidated figures** (`ConsolidatedService`) apply the same trim over the whole tree. People whose names or aliases match count as one person. - **Audit side effects**: every figure change writes `ROLLUP` and `TOTALS` lines, then `ALERT` when a due-total crosses the **alert threshold**. Changing today writes `SCORE` lines (when the score log is on) and `SNAPSHOT` lines. ## What is frozen, and when - **Settle / approve** fixes `settledDue` = the shown due then (stated figure or live figure, late charge included). Settling "as of" a date uses `SheetHistory.asOf`. - **Resettle** (steward) re-fixes it as if the claim were OPEN and unbound now. - **Voiding a SETTLED claim** keeps the figure but takes it out of the totals, and audits `reversed=`. - **A statement** binds every counting claim to its floored figure (`statedFigureOf`) and its shown due. Its due-total is capped, and its date can be an earlier as-of date. **Cancelling the last statement** (steward) unbinds those claims. - **Closing a period** fixes: - its total; - each person's total: claims due in it, counted by their status at the end of the period's last day; - each person's **carried** figure: claims due in earlier periods that were still open then, plus the **opening balance**; - each pool member's cut. These stay fixed until the period is reopened. ## Who may do what - **Roles**: CLERK (the default), STEWARD, VIEWER, RESTRICTED (acts as a clerk but sees only their crews' people). A **delegation** makes a user a steward while today is inside its date range. - **Permission matrix** (`Action`), with standing defaults: - OPEN, SETTLE, VOID, CLOSE, TODAY: clerk, steward, restricted; - REASSIGN, REOPEN: steward only. - **Steward-only, hard-coded**: waive, redate, set due-by, review, assign review, resettle, void a SETTLED claim (only within 7 days of its first SETTLED log date), flag a person, cancel a statement, lock/unlock a period, rollover and undo, archive, transfer, merge, withdraw a rate. - **Self-settle rule**: whoever opened or last edited a claim can't settle or approve it. - **Clerk limit**: a clerk's settle of a due above the **clerk limit** goes to PENDING instead. The limit is the grade's own, else the sheet's, in force on the claim's date; n/a is within any limit. - **Approve / reject a PENDING claim**: a steward, or the person's **approver**. - **Flagged person**: while the flag runs (until `flagUntil`), only a steward may open their claims. - **Viewers, archived sheets, as-of screens**: every change is refused by guards. Bulk actions refuse each claim instead. - **Editor lock**: held per user, and only for the current sheet-today. ## Gates on open and settle - **Open**: - `refuseNoteless`: blank note with due above the **note threshold**; - `refuseOverCap`: the period's per-person **claim cap**; - `refuseOverMaxOpen`: the sheet's **max open**; - above the **review threshold**, the claim goes to REVIEW instead of OPEN. - **Settle**: `refuseUnproved` refuses when there are no proofs, or no proof of each listed **proof kind**, and the due is above the **proof threshold** (the grade's own, else the sheet's). - **Corrections**: must name a SETTLED claim of the same person, and may be no more than what remains of it. - **Retirement**: a claim can't be dated after `retiredFrom`, or inside a past retirement window. ## Closed periods, holds, imports - **Hard-closed period**: refuses every change to a claim whose due-by (or new due-by) falls in it. Proofs, comments, hold, waive and share still go through. A **soft-close** fixes the figures but allows changes, and marks new claims as late entries. - **Automatic close**: changing today closes periods that are more than the sheet's **grace days** past their end. A **locked** period can't be reopened. - **Person hold**: changes no claim total. It only zeroes the person's **pool cut** while it covers today. - **Pool cuts**: pot × share ÷ shares, HALF_EVEN, with the remainder going to the smallest non-zero cut. Retired or held members get 0.00, and an unbalanced pool (≠ 100.00) gets no cuts. Crews are pools with equal shares. - **Imports** are all-or-nothing: - **people** (`name,grade,terms,contact`): matches update the person, grade from today; - **rates**; - **claim paste**: adds and opens each claim; a match on person, date and note updates a DRAFT's amount; a `#ref` suffix sets the reference; - **opening balances** (`name,period,amount`): added to the carried figure. - **Rollover**: makes the next fiscal year's periods, adds each person's open figure to the first new period's opening balance, and soft-closes the old year. - **Plans** generate DRAFT claims up to today. ## Inconsistencies I found while reading - **Waiver shown wrongly**: the screen's `lateChargeCents` ignores `waived`, so a waived overdue claim still shows a late charge, while the server's figures and audit lines give none. - **Stale hold comments**: the header comment in `people.ts` and the `isOpen` comment both say a hold takes OPEN/PENDING claims out of the totals. The code on both sides keeps them in. - **Terms date**: the class Javadoc says terms are "in force on its date", but the code uses the terms in force on the sheet's today. - **Holiday re-fix**: it recomputes from the claim's current `date`, not `dueFrom`, so a re-dated claim moves when a holiday is added. - **Misplaced Javadoc**: the comment for `refuseOverCap` sits above `refuseOverMaxOpen`. # 2. How hard it was Hard. The core maths is in `RollupService`, but the counting rules, freezes and permissions are spread across about 15 services, hard-coded role checks, guards and a database-backed permission matrix. The front end keeps its own parallel copy of the figure rules, and the two have already drifted apart (the waiver, the stale hold comments), so a new developer can't trust any one place, and has to check behaviour against the code rather than the comments.
